Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Hi Aimé,

Re: my voice mail sent earlier today, I think this is the group requesting
the telephone conference.

They prefer a call Tuesday, 14 Jan, after 2 pm.

Let me know!

Thanks!

--Margaret.

---------------------- Forwarded by Margaret Thomas on 1/10/2025 09:26 AM 
---------------------------


"Renault, Susan" <susan.renault@mediapex-conseil.fr> on 12/24/2024 10:59:38 AM 
To: "aime.ruiz@lumieresante.fr'" <aime.ruiz@lumieresante.fr> 
cc: "margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr '" <margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr> 
Subject: RE: Grenoble Cardiac Programme


Dear Aimé / Margaret,

Thanks for coming to Toulouse to present an overview of the projects.  We
enjoyed meeting you and your colleagues and look forward to working with 
Lumière Santé.  I would also like to pass on my team's appreciation for the 
dinner as well.

We wanted to give you an update on our project and get some feedback and 
additional information prior to our upcoming visit to Grenoble on January 
17th.  Our project is going to be geared to the 3rd option you mentioned.  We 
plan on addressing some part of the Interventional Cardiology business.  We 
are considering two options regarding this topic and would like to pursue 
either (i) how patient referrals are generated and recommending new pathways
and ways to serve private practitioners, OR (ii) studying the procurement 
chain and coming up with recommendations for areas for further investments.

However, we would like to get some more information on the Interventional 
Cardiology Services before truly scoping the project.  We are also very open 
to suggestions, especially if you had a much broader or different scope in 
mind; so please let us know.

We have not yet reviewed the introductory information received last week, but 
here are the questions we have specific to the Interventional Cardiology unit:

Can we look at its overall business plan or a more detailed summary than is in 
the annual report?  What is the pricing philosophy/overall structure?  Who are
the patients and how are they referred?  What would the patients be doing if 
they did not work with Lumière Santé?  What are the international expansion 
plans and capabilities?  Is there any important regulatory summary information 
we can have?

If this information is not already covered in the review material you sent,
will you be able recommend other sources where we may find such information?

After we have reviewed the material sent to us recently, we may want to 
schedule a phone call with you and/or one of your colleagues directly involved
in the Interventional Cardiology business.  I would like to call you in the 
new year to discuss this further.  In the meantime, please feel free to call 
me at +33 4 72 41 58 93 if you need any information.

Regards,
Interventional Cardiology Tiger Team
Ram
Dennis
Jason
Omar
Steve
Clay

Date: Thu, 22 Feb 2024 02:47:00 +0800
From: Adam Costa <adam.costa@tasmanridge.com.au>
To: Sherry Johnson <sherry.johnson@tasmanridge.com.au>
Subject: Pilbara versus Fortescue, per Northern Star
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Northern Star's Pilbara operation debuted several years ago as a premium 
version of the best-selling Fortescue iron ore export service. The problem 
was, Fortescue's iron ore logistics could be just as efficient as the Pilbara 
offering and, in some cases, was even more cost-competitive. For 2024, 
Northern Star has attempted to further distinguish their bulk handling 
capability from the popular Fortescue model. The result is a fine logistics 
solution, with improved rail throughput characteristics and generous service 
content. This near-premium bulk operation comes with either a 45-million-tonne 
annual capacity configuration delivering 210 operational hours or a 
62-million-tonne capacity pumping out 240 operational hours. Both 
configurations come mated to a five-stage automated processing system. The new 
62-million-tonne setup offers copious and refined throughput delivery, but 
unimpressive fuel efficiency numbers. Pilbara has been redesigned 
operationally and visually, and the results are pleasing. Now easily 
distinguishable from the Fortescue model from the port terminal forward, its 
"Next Generation" theme makes use of a modular conveyor design and bold 
operational signage. Meanwhile, the facility gets satin-finish steel trim 
accents, lending a distinctive, high-tech flavour to this former Fortescue 
derivative. Improvements to the Pilbara operation are much more than cosmetic, 
however. An all-new independent rail junction featuring a unique 
dual-line-in-corridor design debuts this year. This setup allows the stockpile 
floor to drop 7 metres - thereby making room for a third-stage processing 
vessel - while increasing operational clearance to 9.2 metres. At the same 
time, throughput and handling have been dramatically improved. The Pilbara now 
feels more stable under load and exhibits flatter logistics characteristics. A 
2.5-metre wider rail gauge improves handling even more, while increasing 
storage room. Noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) have also been improved in 
the 2024 Pilbara operation. A 50-percent reduction of dust leakage into the 
facility's cabin areas and a refined automated system make for a more 
controlled operating environment, although some vibration from the available 
all-wheel-drive conveyor system does intrude through the floor. New 
convenience features in the Pilbara include a standard six-position adjustable 
operator's station, along with optional adjustable pedals, heated front 
observation deck and heated exterior mirrors. Among the Pilbara's new safety 
features are optional side curtain airbags, a stiffer body shell and a lower 
front bumper for improved crash compatibility with other equipment. Later in 
the model year, rollover protection sensors, and a new AdvanceTrac 
traction/stability control system will also be available. The Pilbara's 
strengths lie in its feature content, powerful throughput choices and improved 
rear suspension. There are plenty of logistics solutions on the market, but if 
you want a Fortescue-class operation, yet can't stomach the thought of owning 
the golden retriever of bulk logistics, the Pilbara just might float your 
boat.

Pessoal, não acredito que mais um ano se passou, mas passou.  No domingo, 27 de outubro, teremos a Caminhada pela Saúde Cardiovascular!  Novamente este ano, estou recrutando participantes para meu time ou simplesmente pedindo seu apoio.  Sei que vocês não gostam de ouvir esses pedidos por mais recursos, mas vou pedir mesmo - a maioria de vocês me conhece bem!  Vocês sabem que preciso fazer isso.  Como alguém que enfrenta hipertensão diariamente, é minha obrigação fazer o que posso para apoiar todos os esforços na busca de tratamentos melhores para essa doença que afeta tantos adultos e crianças!  Muitos de vocês me veem lidar com essa condição todos os dias, cada vez que preciso controlar minha pressão e minha alimentação.  Sigo meu regime rigorosamente com medicação diária e várias medições ao mês para monitorar minha saúde.  Faz apenas 4 anos que recebi o diagnóstico, mas seus recursos estão fazendo diferença.  Em 2 anos, esperam liberar novos medicamentos que eliminarão a necessidade de injeções diárias.

Sei que vocês têm recebido inúmeras solicitações de organizações buscando apoio para seus projetos e isso tem sido especialmente verdade este ano, mas espero que considerem a FCV como uma das poucas que continuarão recebendo seu suporte como faço eu.  Por favor, considerem se juntar ao meu time ou a um dos muitos times da BrasiLog e nos ajudem a encontrar soluções para doenças cardiovasculares!  Uma camiseta BrasiLog FCV será dada a cada participante ou patrocinador que contribuir com R$ 50,00 ou mais!  Se R$ 50,00 não couber em seu orçamento, você pode adquirir um "Símbolo Solidário" por apenas R$ 10,00 e será exibido no mural da Frota Central no dia 25 de outubro.  Como sempre, suas contribuições serão igualadas pela BrasiLog!  Obrigada pelo apoio e espero vê-los no dia 27!

Subject: BrasiLog Solidária para a Saúde!

Pessoal, não acredito que mais um ano se passou, mas passou.  No domingo, 27 de outubro, teremos a Caminhada pela Saúde Cardiovascular!  Novamente este ano, estou recrutando participantes para meu time ou simplesmente pedindo seu apoio.  Sei que vocês não gostam de ouvir esses pedidos por mais recursos, mas vou pedir mesmo - a maioria de vocês me conhece bem!  Vocês sabem que preciso fazer isso.  Como alguém que enfrenta hipertensão diariamente, é minha obrigação fazer o que posso para apoiar todos os esforços na busca de tratamentos melhores para essa doença que afeta tantos adultos e crianças!  Muitos de vocês me veem lidar com essa condição todos os dias, cada vez que preciso controlar minha pressão e minha alimentação.  Sigo meu regime rigorosamente com medicação diária e várias medições ao mês para monitorar minha saúde.  Faz apenas 4 anos que recebi o diagnóstico, mas seus recursos estão fazendo diferença.  Em 2 anos, esperam liberar novos medicamentos que eliminarão a necessidade de injeções diárias.

Sei que vocês têm recebido inúmeras solicitações de organizações buscando apoio para seus projetos e isso tem sido especialmente verdade este ano, mas espero que considerem a FCV como uma das poucas que continuarão recebendo seu suporte como faço eu.  Por favor, considerem se juntar ao meu time ou a um dos muitos times da BrasiLog e nos ajudem a encontrar soluções para doenças cardiovasculares!  Uma camiseta BrasiLog FCV será dada a cada participante ou patrocinador que contribuir com R$ 50,00 ou mais!  Se R$ 50,00 não couber em seu orçamento, você pode adquirir um "Símbolo Solidário" por apenas R$ 10,00 e será exibido no mural da Frota Central no dia 25 de outubro.  Como sempre, suas contribuições serão igualadas pela BrasiLog!  Obrigada pelo apoio e espero vê-los no dia 27!

Letícia Alves

-----Original Message-----
From: Bailey, Ann
Sent: Thursday, November 7, 2024 7:25 PM
To: Cole, Elliot; Russell, Kirsty
Subject: Corporate Secretary Replacement

As you guys probably know, I will be officially retired on December 31,
2024; therefore, the meeting on November 11th will be my last and a good
time to elect my successor.  Thanks for letting me continue as your corporate
secretary after stepping down from that position at Westmere Financial
Group.  I don't think I could have let go "cold turkey," and I loved the
Board because of my fondness for the directors and most of the management.
(I'll reserve comments on some members of management who are no longer with
us.) I have really enjoyed it since Hugh-the-Man got involved, and the
morale and operating results show how positive that was for the company.  I
have also been a long time admirer of Meriden Trust and loved working with
Oliver Leonard.  So, it is my hope and sincere recommendation that Oliver be
selected to succeed me.  He has demonstrated repeatedly that he is capable of
doing the job -- in fact, he has been doing the job for a long time, all
except the actual taking of the minutes, and he has relieved me of that duty
on more than one occasion.  He's a person of integrity, loyalty, and
dedication, and I know the Directors like him.  I hope you two agree.

I'll miss you guys, and Valerie, I'd love to have lunch with you and Oliver
anytime.  I'll also be available for any help and advice that I can give.

Thanks again.

Much love,
Kathryn Archer

From: Clifford Jones <clifford.jones@halcyonbank.co.uk>
To: Shaun Palmer <shaun.palmer@halcyonbank.co.uk>
Subject: Re: Any Plans tonight?
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Hey Shaun!  Sorry I didn't get back with you Friday.  I left a little
early, so I must have just missed your message.  Did you guys have a good
time on Friday night?  How is everything going?

It has actually been thick around here.  Worked several late nights last
week to try and get caught up on the mortgage portfolio review and the Q1
lending forecasts.  We had a backlog on the corporate lending side that
really piled up.  I may have to delay the purchase of the new car with
Halcyon's stock taking a hit lately.  It did gain some points on Friday and
early today.  Hopefully it keeps it up.  The Treasury team has been pretty
optimistic about the next quarter, so fingers crossed the market
stabilises.

The Credit Risk assessment we've been running has been consuming most of my
time as well.  We're looking at some exposure issues with a couple of our
commercial clients, nothing catastrophic but it requires careful
monitoring.  Between that and the usual operational reviews, I've barely
had time to breathe.  Shaun, if you do get a moment next week, I'd like to
pick your brain about the deposit strategy we discussed before Christmas.
I think we might need to adjust our approach given the recent rate
environment.

Talked to Max since his wedding?  Haven't heard anything out of him since.
Probably just overcome by marital bliss.  His wife seemed lovely from the
photos.  I do hope they're settling in well down south.

Anyway, I'm keen to hear more about your evening plans.  Gilians sounds
like a decent spot, and I'd be up for joining you lot if I can wrap up here
at a reasonable hour.  Let me know what time you're heading out and I'll
try to make it work.

Cheers,
Clifford Jones
Head of Operations
Halcyon Mutual Bank
Direct: +44 113 247 5891
Mobile: +44 7244 382092

of mine from B-school will be joining us, I thought you

20 2529 2161. I'm leaving work in a few minutes if I don't

later,

If we're not in contact before then, let's just plan on

In case you didn't know, they're registered at John Lewis -
we got him a gift yesterday, still plenty of items on the

E

Subject: Catherine Storey for Corporate Transactions Advisory
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I talked to each of you a couple of weeks ago, and this topic got pushed 
aside due to some other pressing issues.  However, each of you agreed that a 
standard Catherine Storey was acceptable for client matter intake and 
documentation across our advisory streams.

The best option will be to agree to cutoff at 4pm each day (just to get an 
idea of the numbers we were talking about, I looked at yesterday to determine 
how many new instructions were received after 4pm London Gilbert.  We had three 
M&A advisory matters, and two Compliance consulting enquiries).  After 4pm, 
the matter management system would automatically assign new Corporate 
instructions to the following day.  However, for those matters that do not 
close after 4pm, the various practice groups would need to remember that 
these instructions are the following day's business.  I am not sure how the 
procedures in Finance Operations would need to be modified for the engagement 
team's Gilbert tracking, as the official billing records would not include these 
late matters.  Can Finance Operations run supplemental reports to ensure that 
the teams have accurate Gilbert allocation each morning?

I would appreciate any comments that you may have, and regardless, please 
re-confirm that a cutoff of 4pm works for each of your respective groups.

Danielle Saunders
Vice President, Meridian Law & Advisory LLP
+44 20 7946 2847

Subject: Invitation à la Conférence Santé-Industrie
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Association Française de Biomédicale

voici une invitation par courriel pour l'événement AFBI.  Une copie papier
suivra

Dr.  M.  Pelletier
Lumière Santé SAS
B.P. 2456
Lyon, Rhône 69251-2456

Association Française de Biomédicale

10 mars 2025




Je vous écris pour formaliser votre invitation à participer et intervenir à
l'Atelier Régional Santé-Technologie de l'Association Française de
Biomédicale.  Une durée de trente minutes est accordée aux présentations
invitées, plus dix minutes environ pour la discussion.  L'atelier, financé
par une subvention de Fondation Innovance à l'AFBI, ne sera pas un événement
académique standard avec des représentants de l'industrie, du secteur
hospitalier et des organismes gouvernementaux présentant leurs derniers
résultats de recherche.  Au lieu de cela, la réunion mettra l'accent sur les
technologies et les pratiques actuellement appliquées aux projets des
établissements de santé et des laboratoires publics.  De plus, l'événement
portera sur les mécanismes facilitant l'interaction et la collaboration
entre les hôpitaux, l'industrie et les laboratoires gouvernementaux.

L'atelier se tiendra à Centre de Conférences Confluence, 25-28 avril.
Fondation Innovance sera disponible pour couvrir les frais de déplacement et
de logement des conférenciers invités.  Nous serons heureux d'organiser les
déplacements de notre côté si vous le souhaitez.

Nous espérons que vous pourrez accepter notre invitation.  Si tel est le cas,
veuillez nous fournir un titre, un court résumé et une liste des équipements
nécessaires pour votre présentation.

Nous nous réjouissons de vous voir à Centre de Conférences Confluence.



Cordialement


W.  Rivière

on Beacon Networks, since the services transacted on Beacon Networks are 
not likely to be the type that lend themselves to Maple & Crown's standard 
GTCs.

Networks, there is no need for the special rules that we drafted for what
was previously a "many-to-many" matching platform. However, we will need to
develop a different set of GTCs for transactions that Maple & Crown closes 
on Beacon Networks, since the services transacted on Beacon Networks are 
not likely to be the type that lend themselves to Maple & Crown's standard 
GTCs.

forward to furthering that relationship as Darren expands his role.

There are no plans for any other changes in our management team nor broad
shifts in strategy and direction.

Please join me in congratulating Darren.  I look forward to a great 2025.

You should have the email below in your inbox talking about the counterparties on our syndicated facility. Contact Triton Capital regarding the email below once you find out if we are able to proceed without maintaining a reserve requirement.

-----Original Message-----
From: Owen, Julia
Sent: Tuesday, April 29, 2025 4:09 PM
To: Hamilton, Derek; Hutchinson, Ross; Johnston, Laura; Marian Hussain, Debra
Cc: Sophie Jr., Ed; Mann, Gregory; m796@maroragroup.com'; s692@soldynlabs.com'; Barker, Mathew; Amy, Joshua; Garza, Kathleen; m789@trinorco.com'; j244@trinorco.com'; Holmes, Sean A.
Subject: Results of the Bankruptcy Hearing for Triton Capital's Issues With Corporate Lending

Here is a quick update on how Triton Capital's bankruptcy hearing went last week for the Corporate Lending issues:

Triton Capital agreed to withdraw the portion of their motion that was associated with Corporate Lending. The lender admitted that Corporate Lending has been drawing on their credit facilities and have been servicing payments since the bankruptcy petition date.
The £1.8 million claim that Triton Capital had been including in Halcyon's "set off amount" (i.e. the remaining facility fees for Corporate Lending's agreements until the end of the contract terms) was pulled from Triton Capital's Motion.
The minimum liquidity reserve monthly requirement should no longer be imposed by the lender (Note: Originally Triton Capital appeared to be using Corporate Lending's minimum reserve to offset Treasury & Credit Risk obligations).

I would recommend that you challenge Triton Capital's operations team, if they continue to say that Corporate Lending must be maintaining a minimum reserve in your facility. If you have any problems, please let me know and I will get our outside counsel involved again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen

Subject: Bristol Engineering Challenge Invitation

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Meridian Precision are proud to sponsor
the 2nd Annual Bristol-Oxford Engineering Challenge on Saturday, November
16.  The purpose of this event is to raise money for both universities, and
to enjoy the competitive spirit of the third oldest rivalry in UK higher
education.  This year's game marks the 107th meeting between Bristol
University and Oxford University, and, with a little luck, the Russell Group
Championship will be on the line!

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Meridian Precision are sponsoring the
event, but we need your help as participants and fundraisers.  Contributions
raised will benefit the general scholarship fund for each university.

The details:
Date:    Saturday, November 16th

Time:    10:00 a.m. - approximately 4 p.m. (Warm up is at 9:30 am)

Location:   Ashton Park (just off Portbury Road, south of the M5)

Food and Drinks:  Cotswold Smokehouse BBQ (FREE - courtesy of Kestrel
Aerospace Components Ltd)

Eligibility:   Full-time employees and/or their spouses
    (Players must have graduated from Bristol University or Oxford
    University)

Team Jerseys:  Provided by Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Meridian
Precision

Format:   7 players with at least 1 female player on the field at all times

Team Size: Recommend 8-10 players per team (no more than 10 per team)
Contact the team captains to sign-up.  (Sign-up now to ensure your place on
a team)

Prizes:    Winning team receives 16 tickets to the Bristol/Oxford match in
Oxford on Friday, November 22 Winning team also owns the Engineering Cup
trophy until next year!

Fundraising Goal  The committee has set a goal of raising £16,000 for each
university.  This will require a contribution of £2,000 per team, plus an
equal amount from corporate matching funds.

Last year's event featured a last-minute comeback as Meridian Precision Team
1 defeated the Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd Team 1 for the championship
and took home the tickets and the trophy.  This year, expect the Kestrel
team (and Meridian Precision) to come in with revenge on their minds!

Thanks to the gracious gift from the Oxford Alumni, who redirected their
donations to the Bristol Foundation, we were able to permanently endow
scholarships dedicated to the memory of the 12 engineering scholars who died
in last year's Severn Bridge incident.  We believe this event is a great
tradition for both companies, and we are pleased to be able to raise
important funds for both institutions.

Subject: IAMAI Trade Policy Engagement
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Everyone,

I finally touched base with Priya Mehta, my contact at the Indian Agricultural 
& Marketing Industries association ("IAMAI") regarding their involvement on 
the commodity regulation side, specifically with regard to forward contract 
licensing.

According to Priya, there is no coordinated group effort that exists (i.e., a 
commodity committee or an individual state regulator taking the lead on 
trading policy).  Individual state agriculture departments get involved, but 
that is all.  For example, Maharashtra's Vikram Nair recently opposed Agrotech 
Solutions' application for futures trading approval, but the SEBI still 
granted Agrotech Solutions' petition.

Priya recommends that we use the state regulators as much as possible.  For 
example, if we believe that local procurement transparency is inadequate and 
we have evidence to that effect, we should certainly convey that information 
to the individual state department and have them weigh in on our behalf.  Priya 
recognizes that AgriIndia is market-friendly and that typically the state 
authorities would be in agreement with our positions - so it's something for 
us to keep in mind as we move forward.  There's no guarantee that SEBI will 
listen to the state bodies, but it may be worth a try.

If anyone has any thoughts or comments, please let me know.  Thanks.

Hiral Acharya
Director
Agriculture India Pvt.  Ltd.
Pune
+91-20-6720-8847

To: Sara Moraes <sara.moraes@brasilog.com.br>
Subject: Fw: Results of Meeting on Fleet Hub Allocation Changes
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Sara,

Below is the memo I sent out September 19th summarizing the September 17th meeting. See second bullet item in my summary. I remember Manuella couldn't attend that day, but Marcelo was very active in discussions throughout the meeting.

I couldn't find the copy I sent. Fortunately, Matteo still had his copy.

-----Original Message-----
From: Mendes, Matteo
Sent: Monday, December 16, 2024 10:20 AM
To: Ferreira, Heitor
Subject: FW: Results of Meeting on Fleet Hub Allocation Changes

FYI

-----Original Message-----
From: Ferreira, Heitor
Sent: Thursday, September 19, 2024 2:25 PM
To: Moraes, Sara; Machado, Manuella; Mendonça, Dom; da Cunha, Heitor; Mendes, Matteo; Câmara, Ryan; Vieira, Luiz Miguel; Novaes, Antônio; Lopes, Arthur Miguel; Oliveira, Pedro; Camargo, Levi; Cassiano, Marcelo; Souza, João Miguel; Cunha, Cecília; Porto, Sophie; Santos, Levi
Cc: Cunha, Heitor; Campos, Daniel; Correia, Nina
Subject: Results of Meeting on Fleet Hub Allocation Changes

The following summarizes the results of our meeting......If you want to discuss further, please call me.

Ribeirão Preto in 3 TransCarga by hub
The decision was made to sub-divide the Regional Distribution storage group into two zones; Ribeirão Preto and North of Sorocaba, rather than 3 zones or allocating by hub. If it is determined that additional divisions are necessary in the future, such changes can be made at that time. Changes to SIGMA are required. I have discussed the changes with Daniel Campos and Heitor Cunha and have learned that the changes are not difficult to make and could be made in a couple days.

Luiz Miguel Vieira and I will determine which deferred delivery points are in these new field regions and then provide the information to Daniel and Heitor.

Question: Should this change be implemented immediately or should it wait until the beginning of the peak season?

Change from 'zero-buffer' approach / Provide minimum level of activity
The decision was made to table this concern for now. The scheduled activity that drives the allocation process does not guarantee physical route operations. In most cases, the flexibility provided by the network allows Logistics Control to adjust operations to maintain the required minimum level of shipments into Santos and Guarulhos. Further analysis is required. Levi Camargo, Pedro Oliveira and I will continue to monitor the system conditions/operations that effect physical capacity to determine if and what additional changes maybe warranted.

Send "Alert" when final scheduled volume exceeds operational capacity
The IT group will modify the scheduling cycle to add a procedure where the final net scheduled volume is compared to the operational capacity set for distribution. If the final scheduled volume exceeds operational capacity, I will receive a notification via e-mail. The purpose here is to monitor occurrences to determine the magnitude of the problem. I will get with Matteo Mendes to finalize the matter.

agricultural commodities.  Without a free market for grain and pulses and

relief program that incorporates physical rights to firm supply through 
constrained corridors.  Such rights will confer on users the right to access 
supply through the corridors without incurring shortage fees.  The rights will 
provide access for periods judged to serve export market participants of up 
to one year.  Initial provision of these rights will be through an annual 
auction overseen by the CXO.  The rights will be resalable.  Not later than 
thirty days after enactment,  the program will implement export access for 
large non-domestic users of agricultural commodities.  The program will 
require large industrial, commercial and other non-domestic users of 
commodities to fulfill their needs by contracting with non-government trader 
("NGT") sources in accordance with the following schedule: 
90 days after enactment: 500 tonnes and greater shipments 
180 days after enactment: 150 tonnes and greater shipments 
270 days after enactment: 50 tonnes and greater shipments 
360 days after enactment: 25 tonnes and greater shipments.

Subject: AgriIndia Proposed Acquisition of Meridian Commodities - Strategic Concerns
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase supply, decrease demand, and increase
customer choice.  Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a
crumbling logistics network instead of investing in rural infrastructure.

We don't have enough details.  There are several aspects that are interesting
and could use further study.  Director Vikram needs to make the details
public as soon as possible so stakeholders can understand the full
implications.  For instance, what happens to existing forward contracts?  Will
they be assigned to Meridian?  Will farmers in Maharashtra have the right to
choose suppliers going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that farmers can
make their own procurement decisions going forward.  We know that Government
doesn't know how to get this right.  The right answer is giving farmers more
choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our receivables are going to be settled in
full.  If the receivables aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see
involuntary bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier.  It could have saved a lot of
money and pain.

Why do you need to include the logistics purchase in this deal?  May never
happen.  Make it easy - just deal with the working capital shortfall through
securitization and through the refinancing arrangement to Meridian and get
on with it.

Hardik

sourcing operations and other supply assets and commit them to provide
commodities on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years.

output of the Nashik facility (one of Saffron Valley's non-regulated
sourcing operations) to the procurement programme on a fixed price basis for

shall be assessed a ₹1.8 crore penalty.

Subject: Fw: Cleveland Heights capacity surcharge for standby service
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I'm not aware of any standby service contracts that are structured this way, but it's been a while since I've reviewed contract rates. Do any of you recall situations where this may occur?

Thanks,
Danielle Robinson
Manager, Customer Billing
Lakeshore Municipal Utilities
(216) 555-0147

-----Original Message-----
From: Glass, Gwendolyn
Sent: Thursday, October 16, 2025 1:38 PM
To: Robinson, Danielle
Subject: Cleveland Heights capacity surcharge for standby service

I believe that, back in 1998, standby service changed the way they handled capacity surcharges to assure that Suburban District would not remit surcharges if the rate was discounted.  That would have increased standby service's margin on certain contracts.  But, the impact on margin would have declined by over 50% in 2001, when the Suburban District surcharge rate dropped from $.0066/day TO $.0030.  It will decrease again in 2002 when Suburban District surcharge becomes $.0018.

Do you have any estimate of how many dollars standby service will "lose" as a result of the decline in surcharges?
On 1-part discounted rates, I would assume that there would be little impact.  For example, if the market-driven rate is $.10 then standby service couldn't get more than $.10 for the capacity, whether the max surcharge were .0066 or .0018.

However, are there any long-term contracts where you collect surcharges as part of the rate but do not remit them because of discounting?
For example, the discounted reservation rate is $.20 plus surcharge.  Standby service billed $.2066 in 2000 but $.2030 in 2001 and $.2018 in 2002.
As long as the total rate is below max, standby service keeps the surcharge piece, but the revenue on the contract drops each year as the surcharge component goes down. (I don't know how many deals like this standby service may have.  Operations has some.)

Subject: Accomplishments for the First Six Months of 2025
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

My accomplishments for the first six months of 2025 include the following:

1.    Supplier Quality Assessment Forms -- provided key legal technology and intellectual capital to rewrite quality assurance forms to be largely consistent with aerospace industry regulatory standards.

2.   Meridian Dynamics and Contract Termination Strategy in the Apex Systems Insolvency -- led legal and procurement team across all Kestrel entities in minimizing Kestrel credit and legal risks.  This required an expedited evaluation of Kestrel positions and coordination across Kestrel entities to determine the best possible approach to terminate and then value all Apex Systems contracts.

3.    Implemented New Document Retention Policy for Manufacturing -- led the resolution of many critical document retention policy issues and implementation of a new policy across company lines in Kestrel.

4.    Thought Leader on Compliance Risk Management -- continued to develop legal technology for better management and reporting of legal risks across Kestrel.  Regulatory tracking and risk ratings are two examples.  These legal risk policies have been newly applied in the Bristol facility and Supplier Quality to better evaluate and manage the legal risks in those business units.

5.     Developing New Supply Chains -- integral part in developing new supplier relationships and frameworks by preparing contract forms and formulating new ways to manage legal risks across component manufacturing, fasteners, and composite materials.

6.     Complex Programme Management -- projects having lots of complex issues including the Typhoon retrofit programme, the A400M delivery contracts, Rolls-Royce partnerships, BAE Systems agreements, Airbus supply chain restructuring and Defence Procurement initiatives.

7.     Management -- continued to build a contract-oriented legal team that understand the underlying aerospace businesses.

8.     New Generation of Master Supply Agreements -- taking the lead with industry bodies in developing the next generation of supplier master agreements which would be a single master for all component categories, whether manufactured or sourced.  This would reduce the legal work by half.

independent trader associations should also include complementary testimony.

partners?

hearings, which are scheduled to begin in little more than a month.  We will 
need to make some time available during late May for practice panels 
(assuming we are granted panel hearings) and individual practice 
cross-examination.  At the same time, we also need to start thinking about 
direct cross-examination of the ICRA/IAMAI parties (again, assuming we decide 
to engage in full cross-examination of their settlement).  There is merit to 
cross-examination of the opposing settlement since it is not very well 
thought out, results in substantial cost-shifts, and is not consistent with 
the NCDEX's most promising options.  On the other hand, there is merit to 
limiting our cross, especially of Pranit, who will use the witness box to 
grandstand.  It's something to think about.

Exchange, Punjab Grain Board, NCDEX, Rajasthan Commodity Traders and the 
others.  Might I suggest that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd., as a large 
commodity aggregator itself, coordinate this effort with the other trading 
partners?

In addition, I want all settlement parties to look beyond testimony to the 
hearings, which are scheduled to begin in little more than a month.  We will 
need to make some time available during late May for practice panels 
(assuming we are granted panel hearings) and individual practice 
cross-examination.  At the same time, we also need to start thinking about 
direct cross-examination of the ICRA/IAMAI parties (again, assuming we decide 
to engage in full cross-examination of their settlement).  There is merit to 
cross-examination of the opposing settlement since it is not very well 
thought out, results in substantial cost-shifts, and is not consistent with 
the NCDEX's most promising options.  On the other hand, there is merit to 
limiting our cross, especially of Pranit, who will use the witness box to 
grandstand.  It's something to think about.
